messages.author: sofia
messages.body: Welcome to the new workspace, everyone. Channels are open by default — keep decisions where people can find them later.

messages.author: jonas
messages.body: Checkout v1 is live. Known debt: the retry state is a bare spinner and the error banner is bespoke — filed for the redesign.

messages.author: marco
messages.body: Payment provider integration notes are in the runbook. The 3DS fallback path is the fragile part — do not touch without tests.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: First draft of the payments migration RFC is up. Short version: we move billing off the nightly cron pipeline onto event-driven processing. Comments welcome on the doc.

messages.author: marco
messages.body: Biggest risk I see is the reconciliation job — if we replay events after a failure we could double-charge.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: Agreed. Proposal: idempotency keys on every charge event, reconciliation only reports, never mutates.

messages.author: amara
messages.body: +1 to report-only reconciliation. Also please budget for provider rate limits during replay — they bite.

messages.author: marco
messages.body: Provider sandbox keeps returning 429s when we replay a full day of events. Anyone seen this before?

messages.author: amara
messages.body: Elevated 429s from the payments provider in production — checkout latency spiking. Investigating.

messages.author: marco
messages.body: Root cause found: burst traffic from the migration replay is eating the provider's rate budget. Throttling the replay now.

messages.author: amara
messages.body: Postmortem drafted. Action items: exponential backoff with jitter on all provider calls, alert on 429 rate, cap replay at 40 rps.

messages.author: sofia
messages.body: Nice turnaround. Let's make sure the migration plan absorbs these lessons before it restarts.

messages.author: amara
messages.body: Same behaviour as incident 4021 — the provider caps bursts around 50 rps. Backoff with jitter fixed it there, see the postmortem.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: Pausing migration work until the incident fallout settles and the backoff work lands. We pick this up again next quarter.

messages.author: jonas
messages.body: New checkout flow mockups are up. Main change: the retry state now tells the user what happened instead of a spinner.

messages.author: tomas
messages.body: These are great — is there a component for the inline error banner or is it bespoke?

messages.author: jonas
messages.body: It's in the shared library as AlertInline. Don't copy the old one from checkout, it's deprecated.

messages.author: jonas
messages.body: Reminder: design critique is Thursdays at 14:00. Bring the checkout retry states, we still owe the payments team a decision there.

messages.author: jonas
messages.body: Welcome Tomas! Ping me if you need a design pass on anything payments-related.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: The migration is back on. RFC updated with the incident-4021 lessons: replay batches at 40 rps with jittered backoff, reconciliation is report-only.

messages.author: marco
messages.body: Summary from today's call: rollout is gated behind a feature flag (payments_v2_rollout). I own the flag config by Friday; Priya updates the RFC with the new cutover date.

messages.author: sofia
messages.body: Good call. One open item: the EU accounts cutover date still needs finance sign-off.

messages.author: amara
messages.body: I'll wire the payments_v2_rollout flag into the 429-rate alert so we catch regressions the moment the flag opens.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: For anyone joining late: the payments-migration RFC lives in Notion under /engineering, and the reconciliation code is in payments-service under reconcile/. Start with reconcile/report.ts.

messages.author: amara
messages.body: The backoff utility landed in libs/retry.ts — use withBackoff() for every provider call from now on. Direct fetch calls to the provider will fail code review.

messages.author: tomas
messages.body: Hi everyone — Tomas, joining the payments team this week. Excited to be here!

messages.author: priya
messages.body: Welcome Tomas! You'll mostly live in #eng-payments — the migration RFC is the best starting point.

messages.author: tomas
messages.body: Reading the RFC now. Where should I start on the reconciliation job?

messages.author: priya
messages.body: Start with reconcile/report.ts — it's report-only so you can't break billing. Elena's sandbox run is the reference dataset.

messages.author: kwame
messages.body: And run the replay locally with the 40 rps cap, the sandbox provider throttles the same way production does.

messages.author: sofia
messages.body: Compensation review numbers for the eng team are in the shared sheet — keep discussion in this channel please.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: Will do. Separate topic: we should discuss Marco's promotion case before the cycle closes.

messages.author: marco
messages.body: Between us — the flag rollout timeline feels tight. I don't want to say it in the channel yet.

messages.author: priya
messages.body: Yeah, I feel it too. Let's raise it Monday with real numbers instead of vibes.

messages.author: chloe
messages.body: Roadmap review moved to Tuesday. Payments cutover is the headline item — bring your open questions.

messages.author: ingrid
messages.body: Reminder from legal: EU customer data must stay in EU regions after the migration. Flag anything that moves data across regions to me before it ships.

messages.author: omar
messages.body: Support update: checkout complaint volume is back to baseline. Closing the ticket batch from the incident.

messages.author: elena
messages.body: Heads up: reconciliation report data looks clean in the sandbox — mismatch rate under 0.01% across 40k replayed events.

messages.author: kwame
messages.body: Nice. I'll add elena's mismatch metric to the cutover-review dashboard next to the 429 alert.

docs.title: Onboarding: your first week
docs.author: ingrid
body: Welcome aboard! This is the one page to keep open. Tick things off as you go — everyone sees this doc, so if a step is stale, fix it for the next person.
## Day one
- [ ] Laptop unboxed, disk encryption on (IT checks this, they will find you)
- [ ] Join #general and say hi — we mean it, people reply
- [ ] Pick your buddy from the People page and book 30 min
- [ ] Read "How we work" (in Docs, right below this one)
## First week
- [ ] Dev environment: clone, `make bootstrap`, green tests locally
- [ ] Ship something tiny — a docs fix counts, the point is the release train
- [ ] Shadow one support rotation hour with Kwame
- [ ] Read the payments migration RFC in #eng-payments (skim is fine)
## When something is confusing
> Ask in a public channel, not a DM. The answer helps the next person, and nobody here thinks questions are a bad look.
Your manager owns your 30/60/90 — expect that doc from them by Friday.

docs.title: How we work
docs.author: sofia
body: Short version: decisions in channels, durable things in docs, meetings only when writing failed twice.
## Communication
- Public channels by default — private is for people topics, not project topics
- Threads for side quests; the channel is the main quest
- A decision that isn't written down didn't happen
## Docs
- Every project gets one living doc, not five dead ones
- Runbooks live here in Docs and get updated *during* the incident, not after
- If you explain something twice in chat, promote it to a doc
## Code
- Small PRs, reviewed within a day — a stuck review is a blocker, treat it like one
- `main` is always shippable; feature flags over long branches
- The person who breaks the build fixes the build (and gets no grief for it)
### Meetings
1. An agenda in the invite, or decline freely
2. Notes land in the project doc before end of day
3. Default 25 minutes — expanding to 60 needs a reason

docs.title: Payments incident runbook
docs.author: marco
body: For provider-side failures on the billing pipeline. Written in anger during INC-4021 (provider rate limits); keep it current — this doc is the on-call's first tab.
## Symptoms
- Spike in `charge.failed` events with `429` in the provider response
- Checkout conversions dropping while traffic is flat
- Reconciliation job report shows growing `pending` backlog
## First 10 minutes
- [ ] Declare it: open an #incident-**** channel, post the graph you saw
- [ ] Flip the flag: `billing.provider_backoff` → aggressive (halves request rate)
- [ ] Page the provider's status page *and* their support — their status page lies first
- [ ] Freeze deploys on the payments services
## Useful commands
bin/billing backlog --since 1h        # how deep is the hole
bin/billing replay --dry-run FILE     # NEVER without --dry-run first
bin/flags set billing.provider_backoff aggressive
## Recovery
Replays are idempotent (charge events carry idempotency keys since the migration) — but reconciliation *reports only, never auto-repairs*. A human signs off on every repair batch.
> Escalation: Priya (pipeline), Marco (provider integration), Sofia (comms to customers). Wake the third one only if the first two are silent for 15 min.

docs.title: Billing migration — cutover checklist
docs.author: priya
body: The last mile of the RFC in #eng-payments. Nothing on this list is optional; if a box can't be ticked, the cutover slips — that's the deal we made after INC-4021.
## Before the window
- [x] Idempotency keys on every charge event (shipped, verified in staging replay)
- [x] Reconciliation job in report-only mode for two full weeks
- [x] 429 alerting wired to the backoff flag (thanks Amara)
- [ ] Load test at 2× Black Friday peak — scheduled with Jonas
- [ ] Provider sandbox contract test green three days running
## During the window (Tuesday, 06:00 UTC)
- [ ] Freeze deploys, announce in #general
- [ ] Flip `billing.pipeline` flag for 1% of traffic, watch for 30 min
- [ ] 10% → 50% → 100%, thirty minutes each, same graphs
- [ ] Reconciliation report clean at every step
## Rollback line
> If the pending backlog exceeds 500 events at any percentage, we flip back. No debate in the moment — we agreed here, in writing, in advance.
Retro doc goes up within 48h either way.
